title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: additive Cheon with planned pair walks and two-hop bucket matching (v3)

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.398 (required 0.39) over the uniform challenge and fresh algorithm coins. It is Cheon's attack in the subgroup H of 2^20-th powers (d = 2^20 divides r-1, 6d divides r-1, A_d is read; only A_1 and A_d are used). Baby and giant scalars are products a*b in H with a a prime of (2^76, 2^76 + 2^70] taken in increasing order and b a class integer <= 2^76 with chi(b) = -chi(a). One algorithmic change over the one-addition-per-point architecture: each class list is planned offline into three-term progressions (x-g, x, x+g) with g <= 2^44 = 16 d^2, and the walk computes [a(x+g)]Q = P+T and [a(x-g)]Q = P-T from the stored midpoint P = [ax]Q and the table entry T = [ag]Q with one shared field inversion, priced as one reference addition plus three extra field multiplications: 2000 + 3*383 = 3149 instructions for two points plus charged second-formula arithmetic; the planned pair fraction is at least f = 0.98 (heuristic H4, measured 0.9815-0.9862 on real toy class lists at matched ratios). Records are 32-byte truncated 192-bit U-orbit keys, matched in direct-mapped head arrays chained through pools at 2^56 owner nodes with 2-hop 512-byte-block FIFO transport (no remote-memory instruction; sender pays fill and post, receiver pays poll and read); candidates are resolved by one bounded linear re-walk of each chain and at most 96 scalar tests, all charged. Total work W(2^20) is at most 2^116.485098 target-group-operation equivalents (exact score 58242549/500000), including both walks and their gap tables, matching and comparisons, transport, plan construction and streaming, the character sieves and base search, candidate handling, the d-th root, the mu_d search and input access. Preprocessing (challenge-independent work) is at most 2^115.5030 units and is included. Peak memory is at most 2^122.6439 bytes; there is no nonuniform advice. Heuristics, all disclosed in proof.md with toy evidence at its stated scope: H1 (coverage |R|/m >= 1 - e^{-K} - 0.0005 at the realized K >= 0.51, supported by an exact census of the construction on toy primes up to m = 2^32 in which every modular and rational coincidence is measured, never excluded by size; the census machinery is validated against independent brute-force field arithmetic), H2 (character equidistribution, affecting only charged small terms, with a stop-and-fail rule), H3 (keys as uniform strings, with every cap and tail bounded and overflow counted as failure), H4 (pair fraction >= 0.98). This is an analytic bound with itemised instruction counts, not a full-size execution.

experiments.purpose: One run with four parts. (1) ledger: recomputes every cost term of proof.md section 6 from exact integers, the exact score with its boundary assert, the preprocessing and memory inequalities, the success inequality with every failure term, and the production algebra identities; arithmetic only. (2) planner: the offline pairing planner of proof.md section 3 on real chi-class lists of toy primes at the production degree parameter GMAX = 16 d^2, sweeping the list span; reports pair fraction, cycle rejections, dependency depth against the cap (evidence for H4). (3) ec: the whole algorithm on a toy j = 0 curve with 2 not in H: planned paired walk with the shared-inversion pair formula, ordered disjoint bases, truncated-key bucket matching with false matches counted, bounded re-walk, six-z resolution, d-th root and mu_d scan; success against prediction, every recovered scalar verified, every sampled collision event checked against the exact coverage of the independently reconstructed emitted sets. (4) census: the exact coverage |R|/m of the construction on a toy prime at the production scaling rule (evidence for H1). Toy parts are evidence at toy scale only.
